pattern.title: Logical Puzzles
pattern.description: Multi-condition logic puzzles. Use sets for shared stimulus.

sets.title: Puzzle 1: 4 friends in a 4-storey building
sets.text:
4 friends (Rajesh, Naveen, Tarun, Ishita) live in a 4-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 4 (top). Conditions:
1. Tarun lives on a higher floor than Rajesh.
2. Ishita lives on the floor immediately above Naveen.
3. Naveen lives on the floor immediately above Rajesh.

sets.title: Puzzle 2: 4 friends in a 4-storey building
sets.text:
4 friends (Kavya, Ishita, Charan, Nisha) live in a 4-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 4 (top). Conditions:
1. Charan lives on floor 2.
2. Nisha lives on the floor immediately above Ishita.

sets.title: Puzzle 3: Stack of 4 coloured boxes
sets.text:
4 boxes of different colours (Red, Blue, White, Yellow) are stacked one above the other. Positions are counted from the bottom (position 1 is the lowest). Conditions:
1. The Blue box is placed somewhere above the Yellow box.
2. The White box is at position 3 from the bottom.
3. The White box is placed directly on top of the Blue box.

sets.title: Puzzle 4: Stack of 5 coloured boxes
sets.text:
5 boxes of different colours (Pink, Black, Yellow, Green, White) are stacked one above the other. Positions are counted from the bottom (position 1 is the lowest). Conditions:
1. The Yellow box and the Black box are placed next to each other in the stack.
2. The White box and the Green box are placed next to each other in the stack.
3. The Black box and the Green box are placed next to each other in the stack.
4. The Pink box is not at the bottom of the stack.
5. The Yellow box is placed somewhere above the White box.

sets.title: Puzzle 5: 5 friends in a 5-storey building
sets.text:
5 friends (Hema, Jagan, Suresh, Kavya, Karthik) live in a 5-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Conditions:
1. Kavya lives on the floor immediately above Hema.
2. Suresh lives on floor 4 or floor 1.
3. Karthik does not live on floor 3.
4. Karthik lives on the floor immediately above Jagan.

sets.title: Puzzle 6: 5 friends in a 5-storey building
sets.text:
5 friends (Venkat, Zoya, Kavya, Lakshmi, Bharat) live in a 5-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Conditions:
1. Exactly 3 floors separate the floors of Zoya and Bharat.
2. Bharat and Kavya live on adjacent floors.
3. Bharat does not live on floor 1.
4. Venkat does not live on floor 3.

sets.title: Puzzle 7: 5 friends in a 5-storey building
sets.text:
5 friends (Meera, Yamini, Chitra, Lakshmi, Prakash) live in a 5-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Conditions:
1. Lakshmi lives on floor 4.
2. Yamini lives on a higher floor than Meera.
3. Prakash and Yamini live on adjacent floors.
4. Prakash and Lakshmi live on adjacent floors.

sets.title: Puzzle 8: 5 friends in a 5-storey building
sets.text:
5 friends (Jagan, Mohan, Manoj, Priya, Bharat) live in a 5-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Conditions:
1. Manoj and Jagan live on adjacent floors.
2. Mohan does not live on the top floor.
3. Bharat lives on an even-numbered floor.
4. Exactly 3 floors separate the floors of Mohan and Manoj.

sets.title: Puzzle 9: 6 friends in a 6-storey building
sets.text:
6 friends (Manoj, Sunita, Bharat, Naveen, Karthik, Anitha) live in a 6-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 6 (top). Conditions:
1. Naveen lives on floor 2.
2. Sunita lives on the floor immediately above Anitha.
3. Anitha lives on the floor immediately above Naveen.
4. Manoj and Sunita live on adjacent floors.
5. Bharat lives on a higher floor than Karthik.

sets.title: Puzzle 10: 6 friends in a 6-storey building
sets.text:
6 friends (Karthik, Charan, Ishita, Chitra, Gayathri, Venkat) live in a 6-storey building, one person on each floor. Floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 6 (top). Conditions:

2. Chitra lives on floor 1.
3. Charan does not live on the top floor.
4. Karthik lives on a higher floor than Venkat.
5. Charan lives on an even-numbered floor.
6. Charan lives on the floor immediately above Ishita.

sets.title: Puzzle 11: 4 lectures between Monday and Thursday
sets.text:
A college schedules 4 lectures (Economics, Chemistry, History, English) on 4 different days between Monday and Thursday, one lecture per day. Conditions:
1. The Economics lecture is not on Monday.
2. The English lecture is held on the day immediately after the History lecture.
3. The History lecture is not on Monday.
4. The English lecture is not on Thursday.

sets.title: Puzzle 12: 4 lectures between Tuesday and Friday
sets.text:
4 people (Omkar, Uma, Priya, Rohit) each have a lecture with a manager, on 4 different days between Tuesday and Friday, at most one per day. Conditions:
1. Uma's lecture is on a later day than Omkar's.
2. Exactly 2 days separate the lectures of Omkar and Priya.
3. Uma's lecture is not on Wednesday.

sets.title: Puzzle 13: 4 lectures between Monday and Friday
sets.text:
A college schedules 4 lectures (History, Biology, English, Economics) on 4 different days between Monday and Friday, one lecture per day, so exactly one day in this period has no lecture. Conditions:
1. Exactly 2 days separate the English lecture and the Biology lecture.
2. Exactly 3 days separate the Economics lecture and the Biology lecture.
3. The History lecture is held on the day immediately after the English lecture.

sets.title: Puzzle 14: 5 lectures between Tuesday and Sunday
sets.text:

1. The Maths lecture is held either on Wednesday or on Tuesday.
2. The Chemistry lecture is held on the day immediately after the Maths lecture.
3. The Chemistry lecture is held on a later day than the Economics lecture.
4. The Computer Science lecture is not on Sunday.
5. The English lecture is held on Saturday.

sets.title: Puzzle 15: 5 lectures between Tuesday and Sunday

sets.title: Puzzle 16: 5 meetings between Monday and Saturday

3. Lakshmi's meeting is on Tuesday.
4. Jagan's meeting is on Thursday or Tuesday.

sets.title: Puzzle 18: 5 visits between Tuesday and Sunday

sets.title: Puzzle 19: 6 lectures between Monday and Sunday
sets.text:

2. The Maths lecture is held on Wednesday.
3. The Chemistry lecture is held on a later day than the History lecture.
4. The Physics lecture is held on Sunday.
5. The Economics lecture is held on the day immediately after the History lecture.

sets.title: Puzzle 20: 6 meetings between Monday and Sunday
sets.text:
6 people (Nandini, Tarun, Farhan, Lakshmi, Chitra, Manoj) each have a meeting with a manager, on 6 different days between Monday and Sunday, at most one per day, leaving exactly one day free. Conditions:

sets.title: Puzzle 21: Ranking of 4 people by wealth
sets.text:
4 people (Madhavi, Hema, Nandini, Sneha) have different wealths. Conditions:
1. Sneha is richer than Nandini, and nobody is between them in wealth.
2. Sneha and Hema are next to each other when the 4 are arranged by wealth.
3. Madhavi is richer than Nandini.

sets.title: Puzzle 1: 3 speakers: who is truthful?
sets.text:
3 villagers of a hill village (Yamini, Anitha, Ramesh) are each either a truth-teller (always speaks the truth) or a liar (always lies). Each makes exactly one statement:
1. Yamini says: "Ramesh and Anitha are both liars."
2. Anitha says: "Yamini is a liar."
3. Ramesh says: "Anitha is a liar."

sets.title: Puzzle 2: 3 speakers: who is truthful?
sets.text:
3 villagers of a hill village (Priya, Ishita, Gopal) are each either a truth-teller (always speaks the truth) or a liar (always lies). Each makes exactly one statement:
1. Priya says: "At least 2 of us 3 are liars."
2. Ishita says: "At least one of Gopal and Priya is a liar."
3. Gopal says: "At most 1 of us 3 is a liar."

sets.title: Puzzle 3: 3 speakers: who is truthful?

3. Jayant says: "Exactly 2 of us 3 are liars."

sets.title: Puzzle 4: 4 speakers: who is truthful?

2. Harish says: "At least one of Sunita and Bharat is a liar."
3. Bharat says: "Exactly 1 of us 4 is a liar."
4. Meera says: "Sunita is truthful."

sets.title: Puzzle 7: 4 speakers: who is truthful?

sets.title: Puzzle 1: choose 4 of 7 with conditions
sets.text:
A firm picks a team for a client project from these employees: Arun, Bhavna, Charan, Deepa, Eshwar, Farida, Gokul. Exactly 4 of them are to be selected. Conditions:
1. If Eshwar is selected, Charan must also be selected.
2. Farida and Arun are either both selected or both left out.
3. Eshwar and Gokul are either both selected or both left out.
4. Exactly one of Eshwar, Arun and Farida is selected.
5. At least one of Arun and Bhavna is selected.

sets.title: Puzzle 2: choose 4 of 7 with conditions
sets.text:
A school chooses a quiz team from these students: Hari, Indira, Jayant, Kavya, Lokesh, Meena, Naveen. Exactly 4 of them are to be selected. Conditions:
1. Hari is selected only if neither Indira nor Kavya is selected.
2. Lokesh is selected only if neither Meena nor Naveen is selected.
3. If Kavya is not selected, then Meena cannot be selected either.
4. Jayant and Naveen are either both selected or both left out.
5. If Meena is not selected, then Jayant cannot be selected either.

sets.title: Puzzle 3: choose 4 of 7 with conditions

2. Qadir and Omkar are either both selected or both left out.

4. If Suresh is selected, Uday must also be selected.

sets.title: Grid puzzle 1: city and hobby of four people
sets.text:
Four friends live in different cities and have different hobbies. The cities are Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Pune; the hobbies are chess, painting, cycling, singing. People: Ravi, Sneha, Kiran, Latha. Each person has exactly one city and one hobby, and no two people share either. Clues:
1. Latha's city is Pune.
2. The person whose city is Kolkata has hobby painting.
3. Sneha's hobby is chess.
4. Kiran's hobby is not cycling.
5. The person whose city is Chennai has hobby cycling.

1. The person whose drink is tea has vehicle scooter.
2. Gita's drink is tea.
3. Salim's drink is coffee.
4. The person whose drink is lassi has vehicle car.
5. Pooja's vehicle is bus.
